Hallintamekanismi, joka erottaa falsifioinnin (faktuaaliset virheet Popperin mukaan) ja mestaruuden tunnistamisen (tietoinen sääntöjen rikkominen Dreyfusin mukaan).
Oletus, että tekoälymallin tuottama päättelyketju heijastaa tarkasti sen todellista sisäistä päättelyprosessia (Jacovi & Goldberg 2020).
Ilmiö, jossa kielimallit perustelevat jälkikäteen intuitiivisesti tuotetun vastauksen, vaikka päättelyketju ei vastaisi todellista prosessia (Creswell ym. 2024; Arcuschin ym. 2025).
Kaksivaiheinen hallintamekanismi, joka koostuu argumentin purkamisesta ja kohdennetusta stressitestistä päättelyn epäuskollisuuden tunnistamiseksi.
Redundanssimekanismi, joka pakottaa useat agentit varmistamaan edellisen agentin päättelyn sisäisen johdonmukaisuuden ennen jatkamista.
Strateginen hallintamekanismi, jossa agentteja ohjeistetaan aktiivisesti ylläpitämään ja raportoimaan erimielisyyksiä konsensuksen välttämiseksi.

Riski, joka syntyy kun eri yleiskäyttöisiä tekoälymalleja käytetään yhdessä ja dataa siirretään niiden välillä, mikä voi vaarantaa datan eheyden siirron tai tulkinnan aikana (vrt. ISO/IEC 25010 2023).
Tekninen kontrolli manuaalisessa orkestroinnissa, jossa käytetään selkeitä alku- ja lopputunnisteita eristämään JSON-objektit muusta keskusteluvirrasta datasiirron turvaamiseksi.

Mekanismi, jossa lähettävä agentti generoi lyhyen yhteenvedon datasta ja vastaanottava agentti varmistaa sisällön vastaavuuden ennen käsittelyä suojatakseen hienovaraisilta merkistö- ja kopiointivirheiltä.
Deklaratiivinen metadata-kenttä JSON-objektissa, joka indikoi suorituksen tapahtuneen erillisessä ympäristössä ja toimii auditoitavana signaalina HITL-varmistuskysymyksen generoimiseksi.
Pysyvä riski, joka kirjataan XAI-raporttiin kuvaamaan manuaalisen orkestroinnin ja semanttisten tulkintaerojen aiheuttamaa mahdollista eheyden vaarantumista.

Ilmiö, jossa kielimallit hylkäävät monimutkaiset normatiiviset ohjeet ja siirtyvät yksinkertaisempaan rationaaliseen maksimointiin kognitiivisen kuormituksen kasvaessa liian suureksi (Kirshner ym. 2025).

Aktiivinen huomionhallintamekanismi, joka pakottaa agentin soveltamaan 'System 2 Attention' -periaatetta (Weston & Sukhbaatar 2023) erottelemalla keskeiset todisteet (Fokus) irrelevantista datasta (Kohina).
Ihmisvalvojan taipumus luottaa epäkriittisesti järjestelmän tuotokseen, mikä voi johtaa alisuoriutumiseen valvontatehtävässä (Parasuraman & Riley 1997).
Käyttötarkoituksen laajentuminen, jossa työkalu muuttuu alkuperäisestä tarkoituksestaan esimerkiksi valvontainstrumentiksi (Koops 2021; AI Now Institute 2021).
Tietoturvastrategia, joka koostuu teknisestä (Vartija-agentti), behavioraalisesta (Kognitiivinen Palomuuri) ja hallinnollisesta (HITL) kontrollikerroksesta.
A conceptual challenge in assessment where trust is built through an auditable reasoning process that manages the tension between reliability and validity (Section 1.3).

Human-in-the-loop oversight where a human supervisor acts as an evaluator to resolve internal tensions and validate the system's performance, requiring tools to identify automation bias (Parasuraman & Riley 1997).
A phase in the scaling strategy where the logic of a hybrid rubric is distilled into a single model using high-quality reasoning data or 'cognitive traces'.
Inter-rater reliability; a measure of consistency between different evaluators (e.g., between the Cognitive Quorum and human experts) often measured using Cohen's Kappa.
A heuristic used to distinguish genuine performances from those that have been overly optimized (Strathern 1997).
A phenomenon where reflection is produced as a performance rather than genuine insight, which the assessment framework must be resilient against (Cullen 2020).

knowledge_base.term: SOLO taxonomy (Structure of the Observed Learning Outcome)
knowledge_base.definition: A framework for evaluating the quality of learning based on the structure of observed learning outcomes (Biggs & Collis 1982).
A statistical framework for evaluating the reliability of measurements (Brennan 2001).
An AI literacy questionnaire developed based on competency models and psychological change- and meta-competencies (Carolus ym. 2023).
A method of assessing student learning by engaging them in real-world tasks (Center for Innovative Teaching & Learning 2025).
A model used to assess chunks in memory, applied here for competence assessment by stimulus matching (Cheng 2021).
A cybersecurity strategy involving multiple layers of security controls (CISA 2016).

knowledge_base.term: Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition
knowledge_base.definition: A model describing the stages through which individuals progress when acquiring a new skill (Dreyfus & Dreyfus 1980).
Theories exploring the interaction between two distinct types of cognitive processing, typically characterized as intuitive/fast and deliberate/slow (Evans & Stanovich 2013).
A paradigm for the design, analysis, and scoring of tests, questionnaires, and similar instruments measuring abilities, attitudes, or other variables (Embretson & Reise 2000).
A theory focused on the role of cognitive effort and the limitations of working memory in fostering the acquisition of complex cognitive skills (de Bruin, van Merriënboer & van Gog 2023).
A new skill for the future of work involving the strategic design of inputs to guide the behavior and output of AI models (Federiakin et al. 2024).
A theory suggesting that individuals have an inner drive to hold all their attitudes and beliefs in harmony and avoid disharmony (Festinger 1957).
A cognitive-developmental area of inquiry focusing on 'thinking about thinking' and cognitive monitoring (Flavell 1979).
A role of Artificial Intelligence in collaboration with humans where tasks are performed by the system without direct human intervention (Fügener, Walzner & Gupta 2025).
A role of Artificial Intelligence in collaboration with humans where AI enhances human capabilities and performance (Fügener, Walzner & Gupta 2025).
Methods used to test language models to identify and reduce potential harms through adversarial testing (Ganguli et al. 2022).
A class of machine learning frameworks where two neural networks contest with each other in a game (Goodfellow et al. 2014).
A security vulnerability where real-world LLM-integrated applications are compromised via external data sources (Greshake et al. 2023).
A research paradigm in Information Systems that focuses on the creation and evaluation of artifacts to solve identified organizational problems (Hevner, March, Park & Ram 2004).
The phenomenon where LLMs generate plausible but incorrect or nonsensical information (Huang et al. 2023).
Statistical uncertainty that refers to the notion of randomness or irreducible variability in data (Hüllermeier & Waegeman 2021).
Systematic uncertainty that refers to the lack of knowledge about the 'best' model or the true state of the world (Hüllermeier & Waegeman 2021).
A framework for exploring interaction in writing, focusing on how writers signal their attitudes and engage with readers (Hyland 2005).
A performance measurement tool that uses specific behavioral examples (anchors) to represent different levels of performance (Jacobs, Kafry & Zedeck 1980; Klieger et al. 2018).
The degree to which an NLP system's explanation accurately reflects the reasoning process used by the model (Jacovi & Goldberg 2020).
A research paradigm that combines quantitative and qualitative research techniques, methods, and concepts into a single study (Johnson & Onwuegbuzie 2004).
Tools used to assess performance based on a set of criteria, often evaluated for reliability, validity, and educational consequences (Jonsson & Svingby 2007).
The process of identifying and understanding cause-and-effect relationships, explored as a new frontier for large language models (Kiciman et al. 2023).
A strategy used at the beginning of a project to imagine that the project has failed, and then work backward to determine what potentially could lead to that failure. (Harvard Business Review 2007)
A measurement tool that uses specific narrative examples of behaviors to anchor points on a rating scale, often used for performance demonstration and progression guides. (Klieger et al. 2018)
The expansion of a process or system beyond its original purpose, often in ways that are unintended or potentially problematic. (Koops 2021)

A set of practices that aims to deploy and maintain machine learning models in production reliably and efficiently, encompassing overview, definition, and architecture. (Kreuzberger, Kühl & Hirschl 2023)

A cognitive bias where individuals with low ability at a task overestimate their ability, often because their lack of competence also robs them of the ability to recognize their own incompetence. (Kruger & Dunning 1999; Nold & Michel 2022)
A framework for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks that combines pre-trained parametric memory with a non-parametric memory (retrieval) to improve model output. (Lewis et al. 2020)
The automatic extraction and identification of argumentative structures within text, such as premises and conclusions. (Lippi & Torroni 2016)

A phenomenon in long-context language models where performance is highest when relevant information is at the very beginning or end of the input context, but significantly lower when it is in the middle. (Liu et al. 2024)

A security vulnerability where an attacker provides specially crafted input to a large language model to override its original instructions or safety guardrails. (Liu et al. 2023; Liu et al. 2024; OWASP Foundation 2025a)
A statistical measure used to examine the agreement between two or more raters or observers. (McHugh 2012)
Descriptive scoring schemes developed by teachers or evaluators to guide the analysis of the products or processes of students' efforts. (Moskal 2000)
A vulnerability in LLM-based systems where a model is granted too much autonomy or access to functions, leading to unintended actions. (OWASP Foundation 2025d)
A specific research methodology for information systems that focuses on the creation and evaluation of artifacts intended to solve identified organizational problems. (Peffers et al. 2007)
A method used to test language models by deliberately attempting to provoke harmful or unintended outputs to identify and reduce harms. (Perez et al. 2022a)
A framework for understanding models, reasoning, and inference related to cause-and-effect relationships (Pearl 2009).
A theory describing the inherent risks and inevitable failures associated with high-risk technologies (Perrow 1984).
The imperative concept that human oversight is essential in AI systems (Pfeifer 2025).
A concept exploring the knowledge that is understood without being openly stated (Polanyi 1966).
An assessment method based on principles of comparative evaluation (Pollitt 2012).
A philosophical critique of certain empiricist beliefs, specifically the analytic-synthetic distinction and reductionism (Quine 1951).
A paradox in management and AI where technology both replaces and enhances human work (Raisch & Krakowski 2021).
A machine learning approach where multiple models are combined to solve a computational problem (Sagi & Rokach 2018).
A bias observed in large language models where preference labeling is influenced by the length of the text (Saito et al. 2023).
An approach to artificial intelligence that incorporates causal reasoning rather than just statistical correlations (Sgaier et al. 2020).
A method for analyzing the structure of connections in cognitive, social, and interaction data (Shaffer et al. 2016).
An autonomous agent framework utilizing dynamic memory and self-reflection (Shinn et al. 2023).
A technique used to reduce hallucinations in conversational AI by retrieving external information (Shuster et al. 2021).
The principle that when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure, often leading to the manipulation of measures (Stumborg et al. 2022).
A dynamic model used to understand how users select products and services based on minimizing effort (Tétard & Collan 2009).
A framework for understanding human judgment under uncertainty, identifying mental shortcuts and systematic errors (Tversky & Kahneman 1974).

knowledge_base.term: Judgment under uncertainty: Heuristics and biases
knowledge_base.definition: A framework exploring how people use mental shortcuts (heuristics) to make decisions and the systematic errors (biases) that result from them (Kahneman 1974).
The process of using natural language processing and computational methods to evaluate the quality of arguments in text (Wachsmuth et al. 2017).
Theoretical structures representing common patterns of human reasoning and argument (Walton, Reed & Macagno 2008).
A specific type of bias identified as a 'blind spot' in large language models (Wang et al. 2023).

The practice of designing assessments specifically to inform and improve student performance rather than just measuring it (Wiggins 1998).
Systems composed of multiple interacting intelligent agents, which can be autonomous or collaborative (Wooldridge 2009).
A failure mode in AI agents where the effectiveness of instructions decreases as the prompt becomes overly crowded (Yeager.ai 2023).

Security vulnerabilities where malicious instructions are introduced to a large language model through retrieved or external data (Yi et al. 2025).
An AI-driven architecture (Soar) that utilizes graph-based structures to organize and execute reasoning steps (Zhang et al. 2024).
Knowledge corruption attacks specifically targeting Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems in large language models (Zou et al. 2024).
A framework for classifying educational learning objectives, specifically referencing the revised Bloom's taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001).
A model for analyzing the structure of arguments, typically consisting of components like Claim (Väite), Grounds (Perusteet), and Warrant (Oikeutus) (Toulmin 2003).
An architecture prioritizing auditability and reliability through a traceable hybrid model, though it often results in higher latency and costs.
An architecture designed for speed and efficiency by reducing latency, at the cost of increased workflow control complexity.
